key_insight: APS-sprayed Cr3C2 on Inconel 625 delivered the strongest hardness and wear-resistance improvement, outperforming Stellite for elevated-temperature tribology.
engineering_relevance: The study shows plasma-sprayed carbide coatings can substantially extend the service life of superalloy components in aerospace and power-generation wear environments.
method: Atmospheric Plasma Spray (APS) applied Cr3C2 and Stellite coatings on Inconel 625 substrates.
Compared coated and uncoated samples using SEM, EDAX, hardness, friction, and wear testing.
Used Taguchi L9 design and ANOVA to identify the dominant wear-performance factor.
evidence_signal: Cr3C2 increased hardness from 505 HV to 720 HV and achieved the lowest wear loss (0.2%) and minimum specific wear rate at 200 °C, while ANOVA ranked coating type as the most influential wear parameter.
watch_item: Results are promising but depend on APS process control and testing conditions, so coating adhesion, thermal cycling durability, and scale-up performance should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Optimization and Tribological Evaluation of Plasma-Sprayed Cr3C2 and Stellite Coatings on Inconel 625 using Taguchi-ANOVA Method
